result.title: One-Shot Calibration via Model Editing
result.summary: Model editing aims to correct errors in large, pretrained models by replacing model generations with user-provided responses. Existing editors assume a single target answer for each edit. However, many real tasks inherently entail uncertainty, resulting in multiple plausible answers with varying likelihoods in user feedback. Such feedback forms a target distribution to not only correct but also calibrate model generations. We therefore propose SoftEdit, the first model editor to leverage uncertainty in user responses and perform one-shot calibration during editing. To generalize calibration to unseen samples, SoftEdit uses co-plausibility relationships between answers while preserving real distributional shifts, balancing the new distributional generality-locality tradeoff. Across three language models, three vision-language models, and two large datasets, SoftEdit achieves state-of-the-art performance, ultimately showing that uncertainty in user responses enables generalizable calibration of pretrained models beyond single-answer corrections.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 SoftEdit，一种模型编辑器：把用户反馈中的多个合理答案视为目标分布，通过答案间的共合理性关系，在一次性编辑中同时纠错与校准，并在通用性与局部性之间取舍；在三个语言模型和三个视觉语言模型上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用分布型目标替代单一答案的监督思路，可能为 LVR 中答案分布监督、贡献分配与校准评价提供可供核查的线索，但不涉及 latent 推理状态或视觉证据使用。
